subtype: Approach: reward budget for small treats [Revision]
passage: My name is Yusuf. In February I decided to be strict with my first salary: no eating out, no small treats, nothing that wasn't a bill. For three weeks it worked perfectly. Then on the last Saturday I walked past a shop, saw a pair of headphones, and bought them without thinking, for far more than a treat should cost. I felt bad within an hour. Trisha listened to me over the phone and said, "You weren't weak, you were starved." She was right. So in March I added a line to the plan: a fun allowance of eight hundred a month, spent on anything I like. I was surprised how much easier the rest of the plan became.

qa.q: What did Yusuf buy on the last Saturday of the strict month?
qa.a: Yusuf bought a pair of headphones for far more than a treat should cost.

qa.q: How did Yusuf feel after buying the headphones?
qa.a: Yusuf felt guilty within an hour, though Trisha said it came from being starved of treats and not from weakness.

qa.q: What could Yusuf do if the fun allowance is spent in the first week, and why?
qa.a: Yusuf could divide it into weekly parts, since smaller portions make the treat last through the month.

qa.q: How might Trisha see the strict plan Yusuf started with?
qa.a: Trisha thought it was too strict, and probably worried that cutting out all fun would lead to a binge.

grounding: After a strict month ended in a binge purchase a person adds a small fun allowance to the plan, making the budget easier to keep.
